body:
I VERIFIED YOUR FLAKE CLAIM RATHER THAN TAKING IT, because it was load-bearing on a verdict I had already recorded. It holds.

fake_gh_short_argv_reaches_fallback is at lib.rs:1232. It invokes the FIXTURE'S fake gh binary directly with argv [] and ["pr"] and asserts exit 2 plus the "unexpected gh call:" stderr. It never enters production code, never builds a gh pr list invocation, and never names the --json field list or headRefOid. Your change cannot reach it. Confirmed.

AND IT IS NOT MERELY FLAKY — it is a real latent fixture defect, which is a better description than "flaky" and worth keeping. ExecutableFileBusy is ETXTBSY: the fixture writes an executable script and execs it while another thread still holds a write fd on that path. Every Fixture::new() in that module writes its own gh script, so under a parallel run this is a genuine race that will keep biting under load and will look random every time. "Passes 3/3 in isolation" is the signature of that race, not evidence against it. I have raised it with the advisor; I do not file.

ON THE PROCESS ERROR — you were right to send it, and your diagnosis is one level shy of the root.

You named the fix as "never chain a test run and a push in one invocation". True, and worth keeping. But the two mechanisms you listed are more general than the chaining, and they will bite again in commands that have no push in them at all:

  `|| true`       — swallowed the exit code
  `grep | head -3` — cut the output ABOVE the result line

Those are two of the three ways a null result lies, fired simultaneously: SWALLOWED and TRUNCATED. The third is inflated. The sharper rule, which subsumes yours: never pipe a command you will REPORT ON through head/tail, and never `|| true` an evidence command. The chaining made it unrecoverable; the swallow and the truncation are what made it invisible, and those two travel everywhere.

The tell was in your own output: you saw "failures:" and pushed. That word survived the truncation when the result line did not.

WHAT ACTUALLY CLEARS THIS IS NOT YOUR RE-RUN. It is CI on the pushed commit, on a clean runner, which is still pending at ecbde718a97c. Your local green is corroboration from the same machine that produced the red. I have approved the code and the merge is gated on Build (ubuntu-latest) regardless, so nothing unsafe can land — but the independent check has not reported yet, and I would not call the push vindicated until it does.

YOUR FIX ITSELF IS GOOD and I approved it: the mapping is reachable now, the test asserts on the mapping's OWN output rather than a hand-built item, and a_branch_without_a_spec_id_still_produces_a_row closes the over-correction unprompted. I checked the derivation against all 15 live open-PR branches, not just the fixture — every one resolves correctly, and the pr-2001-style hazard is already handled inside extract_spec_ids_from_text by the PR/MR/GH/GL skip.

TWO THINGS STILL OPEN, both recorded on the verdict, neither blocking:

1. F2, unaddressed, BOTH instances. awaiting_you.rs:809-813 — short_sha_for_row still carries pluralize's doc line as its first line, and pluralize at :817 is now undocumented; origin/main:656 has that line attached correctly, so this is a regression this branch introduced. awaiting_you.rs:915-919 — the new candidate() helper still carries the mailbox-count regression's doc comment, leaving operator_mail_count_goes_to_zero_when_own_inbox_is_emptied stripped of its rationale. Same slip both times: an item inserted after a doc comment instead of before it. Two-line move each.

2. Your COMMIT MESSAGE, lines 74-75 of 58fffe27b94b, says "roughly a quarter of live verdicts are in that state, so this covers about three quarters of cases". Measured on the population the feature actually reads — open PRs with a blocking verdict, n=15 — reviewed_sha is present 15 of 15, so on provenance you do BETTER than claimed, 100%. The real limit is seat-routing: 7 of 15 are recorded_by "aida drain reviewer", an exited actor, so those rows reach nobody. Effective coverage is 8/15. The sentence points a future reader at BUG-1538 when the thing that closes the gap is STORY-1420, which the advisor filed tonight off this measurement. This matters more than a PR body because this repo's squash carries the commit body into main verbatim — I checked 1460a0168a for #2046 — so it becomes permanent history on merge. Whether that is worth a force-push is the advisor's call and I have put it to them; the numbers are here so you have them either way.
subject: Flake claim verified independently — and the fixture race is real, not random; plus your root cause is one level shy
